q: The phrase ”nouveau riche” means-
e: 'Nouveau riche' is a French phrase meaning 'new rich'. It refers to people who have recently become wealthy, often used with a hint of showing off.

q: What would be the best antonym of ”hibernate”?
e: 'Hibernate' means to spend the winter in a deep, inactive sleep, as some animals do. Its opposite is being active and lively, so 'liveliness' is the best antonym. 'Dormancy' and 'sluggishness' are close in meaning to hibernation.

q: I am in the process of collecting ”material” for my story. the quotation word is a/an-
e: In the sentence, 'material' is the object of the verb 'collecting'. It names the things being collected for the story, so it is a noun.

q: Depression is often ”hereditary”. Here the quotation word is a/an-
e: 'Hereditary' describes the noun 'depression', telling us that it can pass from parents to children. A word that describes a noun is an adjective.

q: Find the odd-man-out-
e: George Eliot is the odd one out because she was a woman writer (Mary Ann Evans) who used a male pen name. Thomas Hardy, Joseph Conrad and James Joyce were all male novelists.

q: Find the odd-man-out-
e: 'The Bluest Eye', 'Sula' and 'A Mercy' are novels by Toni Morrison. 'As I Lay Dying' was written by William Faulkner, so it is the odd one out.

q: Fill in the blank of the following sentence with the right form of verb. If I ____ a king!
e: For an unreal wish, the subjunctive "were" is used with all subjects. So "If I were a king!" is correct.

q: Tiger : Zoology : : Mars : ____.
e: Zoology is the study of animals like the tiger. In the same way, Mars is studied in Astronomy, the science of heavenly bodies. Astrology is not a science.

q: Maiden speech means-
e: A maiden speech is the first speech made by a person, especially a new member of parliament.

q: N.B. stands for-
e: N.B. stands for the Latin phrase "Nota bene", meaning "note well". It draws attention to an important point.

q: What is the masculine gender of ”mare”?
e: A mare is a female horse. The male horse is called a stallion.

q: Botany is to plants as Zoology is to-
e: Botany is the study of plants, and Zoology is the study of animals.

q: Pick appropriate preposition for the following sentence: Noureen will discuss the issue with Nasir ____ phone.
e: "By phone" shows the means of communication, like "by post" or "by email". "Over the phone" and "on the phone" are also used, but they need the article "the".

q: Put the appropriate preposition for the sentence below : Some writers sink ____ oblivion in course of time.
e: "Sink into" means to pass gradually into a state. So writers "sink into oblivion", meaning they are forgotten over time.

q: ‘Call to mind’ means-
e: "Call to mind" means to remember or recall something.

q: ‘Pass away’ means-
e: "Pass away" is a polite way of saying "die".

q: Pick the word that is synonymous with ‘authoritarian’.
e: Authoritarian means demanding strict obedience and not allowing personal freedom. Autocratic, meaning ruling with absolute power, is the closest synonym.

q: The word ‘permissive’ implies-
e: Permissive means allowing a lot of freedom, often more than usual. So it implies being liberal. Submissive means obedient, which is a different idea.

q: Pick the correct part to fill in the gap of the following sentence : Each of the sons followed- father’s trade.
e: "Each of the sons" is singular, and sons are male. So the matching pronoun is "his": Each of the sons followed his father's trade.

q: ‘Subject-Verb Agreement’ refers to-
e: A verb must agree with its subject in number (singular or plural) and person (first, second or third). English verbs do not change form for gender.

q: The only error in the sentence ” One of the recommendation made by the committee was accepted by the authorities” is-
e: After "one of", a plural noun is used. So "recommendation" should be "recommendations": One of the recommendations ... was accepted.

q: ‘The French’ refers to-
e: "The" with a nationality adjective like French refers to the people of that nation as a group. So "the French" means the French people.

q: If a person cannot stop taking drugs, he or she is-
e: To be addicted to something means one cannot stop using it. So a person who cannot stop taking drugs is addicted to them.

q: The word ‘officialese’ means-
e: Officialese is the formal, wordy language used in official documents and offices. The suffix "-ese" here refers to a style of language, as in "journalese".

q: The verb ‘succumb’ means-
e: To succumb means to give in or submit to a force or pressure. Achieve, win and conquer have opposite ideas.

q: Fill in the blank with the appropriate part: We look forward ____ a response from you.
e: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund (-ing form). So "look forward to receiving" is correct.

q: If a part of a speech or speech or writing breaks the theme, it is called-
e: Digression means moving away from the main subject in speech or writing. Anti-climax is a disappointing end after a build-up.

q: The expression ‘take into account’ means-
e: "Take into account" means to consider something when making a judgement.

q: Choose the best translation of ‘কর্তৃপক্ষ তাকে তিরস্কার করলো’ from the alternatives below-
o: The authorities took him to book.
The authorities took him to task.
e: "Take someone to task" means to scold or criticise someone strongly. So it best translates "তিরস্কার করলো". "Take to book" is not standard; the idiom is "bring to book", meaning to punish.

q: ”Such claim needs to be tested empirically” suggest that-
o: The test should be based on assumption.
The test should be based on idea.
The test should be based on experience.
The test should be based on calculation.
e: Empirical means based on observation and experience rather than theory. So testing a claim empirically means the test should be based on experience.

q: The idiom ”put up with” means-
e: "Put up with" means to tolerate or bear something unpleasant.

q: In many ways, riding a bicycle is similar to-
e: "Riding a bicycle" is a gerund phrase, so it should be compared with another gerund phrase, "driving a car". This keeps the sentence parallel.

q: Choose the correct synonym for ‘Extempore’-
e: Extempore means spoken or done without preparation. Impromptu has the same meaning. Planned is the opposite, and Improvise is a verb, not a synonym of the adjective.

q: What is the most appropirate synonym of the word,Menacing’ from the options below:
e: Menacing means threatening or suggesting danger. Alarming is the closest meaning. Encouraging, Promising and Auspicious all suggest something good.

q: Choose the correct antonym for ‘Oblige’-
e: To oblige means to help someone by doing a favour. To bother means to trouble or inconvenience someone, which is the opposite. Bind and Require are related to the other sense of oblige, "to compel".

q: ‘Cynical’
e: Cynical means distrustful of people's sincerity. Gullible means too ready to believe others, so it is the opposite. Pessimistic is close in meaning to cynical.

q: Select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the given sentence: ”We were no more surprised than Rahman”.
o: We were less surprised than Rahman.
Rahman was less surprised than us.
We were as surprised as Rahman.
e: "No more ... than" means the two parties are equal in that quality. So the sentence means we were as surprised as Rahman.

q: Not once has our neighbour invited us into his house.
o: Our neighbour has invited us into his house not once but many times.
Our neighbour has never invited us into his house .
Occasionally our neighbour has invited us into his house .
Our neighbour has not always invited us into his house .
e: "Not once" is an emphatic way of saying "never". So the sentence means our neighbour has never invited us into his house.

q: Choose a suitable word/phrase to fill in the blanks of the given sentence : Travellers ____ their reservation well in advance if they want to visit the St. Martin’s island.
e: "Had better" is followed by the bare infinitive, without "to". So the correct form is "had better get".

q: After food has been dried or canned ____ for later consumption.
e: The main clause needs both a subject and a verb. "It should be stored" supplies the subject "it" (the food) and the verb. The other options lack a proper subject.

q: Choose the word/phrase that best retains the meaning o f the underlined word/phrase in the given sentence: Despite being a brilliant scientist, he does not seem to ”get his ideas across”.
e: "Get one's ideas across" means to make others understand one's ideas. So "make his ideas understood" keeps the same meaning.

q: What may be considered ”courteous” in one culture may be arrogant in another.
e: Courteous means polite and respectful. Gracious has a similar meaning. Coarse means rude, and flimsy means weak.

q: Identify the incorrect word/phrase indicated by (1), (2), (3) or (4) in the following sentence: ”Every” man or woman ”should” vote ”for” the candidate of ”their” choice.
e: "Every man or woman" is a singular subject, so the pronoun should also be singular, "his or her". Using the plural "their" is the incorrect part in formal grammar.

q: Identify the incorrect word/phrase indicated by (1), (2), (3) or (4) in the following sentence: A doctor may be able ”to diagnose” a problem ”prefect” but he may not able to find a drug ”to which” the patient ”will respond”.
e: An adverb is needed to modify the verb diagnose, so "perfect" should be "perfectly". The word given in the question is also misspelt as "prefect".

q: Identify the incorrect word/phrase indicated by (1), (2), (3) or (4) in the following sentence: According to experts a good way ”to” ”improve” listening skills is ”by” ”watch” television, specially news and documentaries.
e: A preposition like "by" is followed by a gerund, not the base form of a verb. So "by watch" should be "by watching".

q: Choose the pair of words that expresses a relationship similar to that of the given pair: Words:writer
e: A writer works with words, just as a baker works with butter as an ingredient. Both pairs show material and the person who uses it.

q: Choose the pair of words that expresses a relationship similar to that of the given pair: Patron:support
e: A patron gives support, just as a counselor gives advice. Both pairs show a person and what that person provides.

q: Choose the pair of words that expresses a relationship similar to that of the given pair: Heart : human
e: The heart is the vital central part of a human, just as the engine is the vital part of a car. Both show a part and the whole it drives.

q: Choose the meaning of the given expressions: “No news is good news”
o: It is likely that we expect bad news.
It is likely to have bad news.
It is likely that nothing bad has happened.
It is unlikely that nothing bad has happened.
e: "No news is good news" means that if we hear nothing, it is likely that nothing bad has happened, because bad news usually travels fast.

q: A bird in hand is worth two in the bush.
o: Take what you have got readily available rather than expecting better in the future.
The seen is better than the unseen.
It is no good beating about the bush.
e: This proverb advises us to value what we already have rather than risk it for something better that is uncertain.

q: The sentence ‘Who would have thought Shylock was so unkind’ expresses-
e: The sentence is not a real question. It expresses surprise that Shylock was so unkind, so it shows wonder.

q: To ‘raise one’s brows’ indicate-
e: To raise one's eyebrows is a facial expression showing surprise or mild shock.

q: In each of the following questions, out of the given alternative, choose the one that best expresses the meaning of the given word : Sporadic-
e: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals or in scattered places. So its closest meaning is Scattered. Consistent, Uniform and Frequent express the opposite idea of regularity.

q: Omnipotent-
e: Omnipotent means all-powerful, having unlimited power. Supreme is the closest meaning. Feeble, Impotent and Vulnerable all suggest weakness.

q: In each of the following questions, choose the word opposite in meaning of the given word: Repeal-
e: To repeal means to cancel a law officially. Its opposite is Enact, which means to make a law. Abolish, Annul and Nullify are synonyms of repeal.

q: Antonym of Equity is –
e: Equity means fairness and impartial treatment. Bias, meaning partiality or prejudice, is its opposite. Uprightness, Justice and Integrity are close in meaning to equity.

q: In each of the following questions, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which can be substituted for the given words/sentence : A formal composition or speech expressing high praise of somebody-
e: A eulogy is a speech or writing that praises someone highly, often after death. An elegy is a sad poem of mourning, and a caricature is an exaggerated drawing.

q: The word ‘Shrug’ indicating doubt or indifference is associated with-
e: To shrug means to raise one's shoulders briefly to show doubt or indifference. So the word is associated with shoulders.

q: Fill in the blanks in the following sentence by selecting the most appropriate alternative : He is quite _____ in dealing with people.
e: Diplomatic means skilful and tactful in dealing with people. The sentence praises his skill, so a positive word fits. Unsubtle, imprudent and impolite are negative.

q: They suffered much ____ tornado had hit their village.
e: Since can introduce a reason, meaning "because". The sentence means they suffered much because a tornado had hit their village. Untill is misspelt, and "as if" and "let alone" do not fit the meaning.

q: One of the four sentences, given below is grammatically wrong. Choose the wrong sentence:
o: The land is belonged to an old lady.
They parted from one another suddenly.
e: Belong is an intransitive verb, so it is not used in the passive voice. The correct form is "The land belongs to an old lady." The other three sentences are correct.

q: One of the four sentences, given below is grammatically wrong. Choose the wrong sentence :
o: He was always arguing with his brother.
His failure resulted for lack of attention.
When will you write to him about your plan?
Who was the boy you were all laughing at?
e: The phrase is "result from", not "result for". The correct sentence is "His failure resulted from lack of attention." The other sentences are correct.

q: Choose the correct spelt word :
e: The correct spelling is Voluntary, meaning done willingly without force.

q: Choose the correct spelt word :
e: The correct spelling is Accelerate (a-c-c-e-l-e-r-a-t-e), meaning to increase speed.

q: Choose the correct spelt word :
e: The correct spelling is Tsunami. The word comes from Japanese, meaning "harbour wave", and the T is silent in pronunciation.

q: Of the four alternatives, find the one that best fits into the blank space : While living in poverty, the poet had to _____ a great deal of sufferings.
e: "Put up with" means to tolerate or endure. A poet in poverty had to endure much suffering, so it fits. "See through", "pass by" and "fall back" have different meanings.

q: Wordsworth introduced the readers ______ a new kind of poetry.
e: The verb introduce takes the preposition "to" before the person: introduce someone to something. So the answer is "to".

q: _____ his earlier study, the Professor’s new study indicates a general warning trend in global weather.
e: The correct expression is "in contrast to", used to compare two different things. Other prepositions with this phrase are not standard.

q: Only those who are not serious to their success work by ____ and starts.
e: "By fits and starts" means irregularly, working in short bursts and then stopping. People who are not serious work in this way.

q: Of the four alternatives given below, choose the word/words that best fits into the underlined word given in the sentence : ‘One day women will have what has so long been denied them – leisure, money and room to themselves’.
e: In the sentence, "room to themselves" means a private space of their own. So Space is the closest meaning. Liberty means freedom, which is a different idea.

q: Choose the word/words that best fits into the underlined word given in the sentence: Crafty men condemn studies, simple men admire them and wise men use them.
e: Condemn means to express strong disapproval. Denounce has the same meaning. Laud, Compliment and Acclaim all mean to praise.

q: The following idiom is followed by some alternatives, choose the one that best expresses its meaning. To end in smoke-
e: "To end in smoke" means to come to nothing, when a plan or hope fails without any result.

q: AMICABLE (Synonym)
e: “Amicable” means friendly and without quarrel, as in an amicable settlement.

q: Opposite word for LIABILITY:
e: In accounts, a liability is what one owes, and an asset is what one owns. So “assets” is the opposite of “liability”.

q: Opposite word for HATE:
e: “Hate” means strong dislike, and “admire” means to regard with respect and liking. “Abhor” and “loathe” are synonyms of hate.

q: In each of the following questions, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which can be substituted for the given words/sentence:- A song embodying religious and sacred emotions _____ .
e: A hymn is a religious song of praise. An ode is a formal poem, and a ballad is a story told in song.

q: Time after twilight and before night –
e: Dusk is the darker stage of twilight just before night. Dawn is the beginning of daylight.

q: Fill in the blanks in the following sentence by selecting the most appropriate alternative from among the four choices given:- Parliamentary democracy demands discipline and _____ to the rules.
e: “Adherence to the rules” means sticking to and obeying them. It is the only noun here that takes “to” and fits the meaning.

q: Reason is the highest faculty ______ on human by their creator.
e: “Bestow on” means to give something as a gift or honour. “Reason bestowed on humans by their creator” fits well; “conferred on” is also possible.

q: Rishan walks as if he ____ lame.
e: “As if” for an unreal situation takes the past subjunctive “were” for all subjects. Rishan is not really lame, so “were” is correct.

q: One of the four sentences given in each question is grammatically wrong. That alternative is your answer:
o: Neither you nor I am in a sound position.
He begged the favour of my granting him leave.
Your action is not in conformity with the law
e: The correct expression is “detrimental to”, not “detrimental for”. The other three sentences are correct.

q: One of the four sentences given in each question is grammatically wrong. That alternative is your answer:
o: He has no desire for fame.
He is too miserly to part with his money.
He has invited me for dinner.
e: “Intend to go” is the more standard form, though “intend going” is also seen in British English. Some also treat “invited me for dinner” as weaker than “invited me to dinner”, so this item is disputed.

q: Each of the following idioms is followed by some alternativeChoose the one which best expresses its meaning :- To keep one’s head-
e: “To keep one’s head” means to stay calm in a difficult situation.

q: To put the cart before the horse –
o: to offer a person what he cannot eat
to force a person to do something
to reverse the natural order of things
e: “To put the cart before the horse” means to do things in the wrong order, reversing the natural order.

q: To read between the lines –
e: “To read between the lines” means to understand the hidden or unstated meaning.

q: In each of the following questions, a sentence has been given in Active (or Passive) voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive (or Active) voice : I know him.
o: He has been known by me.
e: Verbs like “know” take “to” rather than “by” in the passive. So “I know him” becomes “He is known to me.”

q: A lion may be helped even by a little mouse.
o: A little mouse may even help a lion.
Even a little mouse may help a lion.
A little mouse can even help a lion.
Even a little mouse ought to help a lion.
e: In the active form, the agent “a little mouse” becomes the subject, and “even” stays with it. Modal “may” is kept, so “Even a little mouse may help a lion” is correct.

q: Choose the correctly spelt word:-
e: The correct spelling is “leisure”, meaning free time.

q: Choose the correctly spelt word:-
e: The correct spelling is “supersede”, meaning to replace. It ends in “-sede”, unlike “precede”.

q: Of the four alternatives given under each sentence, find the one that best fits into the blank space :- The horror movie scared them out of their ______.
e: “Scared out of one’s wits” means extremely frightened.

q: The people who carry a coffin at a funeral are called ________.
e: Pallbearers are the people who carry or walk beside a coffin at a funeral. Undertakers arrange funerals, and mourners grieve.

q: Honey is ____ sweet.
e: “Very” is used before an adjective to make it stronger in a neutral sense. “Too” or “much too” suggests more than is wanted, which does not suit honey being sweet.

q: Your conduct admits ____ no excuse.
e: “Admit of” means to allow or leave room for. So “Your conduct admits of no excuse” is correct.

q: I shall not ____ the examination this year.
e: In formal English we “appear at” or “sit for” an examination. Only “appear at” is given complete among the choices.

q: They travelled to Savar-
e: The fixed phrase is “on foot”. We say “by bus” or “by car”, but not “by foot”.

q: He said that he ____ be unable to come.
e: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb, “will” changes to “would”. So “he said that he would be unable to come” is correct.

q: Neither Rini nor Simi ____ qualified for the job.
e: With “neither … nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Simi” is singular, so “is” fits.

q: He said that he ____ the previous day.
e: “The previous day” shows an action before the past moment of speaking. So the past perfect “had come” is correct.

q: He watched the boat ____ down the river.
e: After verbs of perception like “watch”, “see” and “hear”, we use object + present participle for an ongoing action. So “watched the boat floating” is correct.
